title: An overview of dexterous manipulation
why: Canonical definition of dexterous manipulation (in-hand object motion by fingers) and the classical model-based taxonomy the survey positions itself against. [SOURCE UNAVAILABLE: publisher paywall, no author-hosted copy found 2026-09-18. Cite by metadata only; no claim in the survey may rest on its contents.]

title: Hands for dexterous manipulation and robust grasping: a difficult road toward simplicity
venue: IEEE Transactions on Robotics and Automation
why: Classic review framing the trade-off between hand complexity and dexterity, the origin of the simplicity/synergy argument. [SOURCE UNAVAILABLE: IEEE T-RO paywalled; no author-hosted copy found 2026-09-18. Cite by metadata only; the overlapping open chapter is bicchi_grasping_chapter_2001.]

title: On dexterity and dexterous manipulation
why: Reviews definitions and measures of hand dexterity (workspace, isotropy, manipulability) and separates hand dexterity from task dexterity, useful for the metrics section.

title: A Century of Robotic Hands
venue: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems
why: Hardware-side historical review of robotic hands (actuation, underactuation, soft hands) that the learning-centred survey can defer to for hand design. [SOURCE UNAVAILABLE: publisher paywall, no author-hosted copy found 2026-09-18. Cite by metadata only; no claim in the survey may rest on its contents.]

title: Sim-to-Real Transfer in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotics: a Survey
why: Standard reference for domain randomisation, adaptation and related sim-to-real methods that dexterous RL pipelines rely on.

title: Foundation Models in Robotics: Applications, Challenges, and the Future
why: Canonical survey of foundation models in robotics; delimits what the dexterous survey does not need to re-cover on VLAs and LLM planners.

title: Dexterous Manipulation through Imitation Learning: A Survey
why: Closest existing survey: covers demonstration collection, retargeting and IL for multi-fingered hands; the new survey must state what it adds (RL, bimanual, evaluation).

title: Interactive Imitation Learning for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation: Challenges and Perspectives -- A Survey
why: Survey of interactive/human-in-the-loop imitation learning for dexterous hands; complements An et al. on the IL side.

title: Towards a Unified Understanding of Robot Manipulation: A Comprehensive Survey
why: Broad manipulation survey (planning, control, data, benchmarks) that treats dexterous hands only in passing; shows the gap a hand-focused survey fills.

title: Towards Robotic Dexterous Hand Intelligence: A Survey
why: Most recent dexterous-hand survey, spanning hardware, methods, data and evaluation; the new survey must differentiate on bimanual coverage and measurement rigour.

title: Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning: Challenging Robotics Environments and Request for Research
why: Origin of the Gym/Gymnasium-Robotics Shadow Hand block, egg and pen tasks that remain the default single-hand RL sanity benchmark.

title: Towards Human-Level Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation with Reinforcement Learning
why: Bi-DexHands: the first two-Shadow-Hand task suite in Isaac Gym with single-agent, multi-agent, offline and multi-task RL baselines; the reference bimanual benchmark.

title: DexArt: Benchmarking Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation with Articulated Objects
why: Benchmark for category-level generalisation of a dexterous hand to unseen articulated objects (faucets, buckets, laptops) from point clouds.

title: RoboHive: A Unified Framework for Robot Learning
why: Consolidates the Adroit hand suites (relocate, pen, door, hammer, TCDM) with real-robot and teleop pipelines; the MuJoCo dexterous benchmark most RL papers report on.

title: HumanoidBench: Simulated Humanoid Benchmark for Whole-Body Locomotion and Manipulation
why: Whole-body benchmark whose humanoid carries two dexterous hands; shows that standard RL fails on most bimanual manipulation tasks, motivating hierarchical methods.

title: DexVerse: A Modular Benchmark for Multi-Task, Multi-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation
why: 100 tasks across 3 arms and 6 dexterous hands with a modular task/asset/embodiment interface; reports poor cross-task and visuomotor generalisation of current policies.

title: Bench2Dex: Benchmarking Visuo-Tactile Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across Dexterous Hands
why: 26 bimanual tasks across 12 hand morphologies with a shared simulated tactile interface, stage-level progress and execution-quality metrics, and seven perturbation types for robustness.

title: Isaac Gym: High Performance GPU-Based Physics Simulation For Robot Learning
why: The GPU simulator behind Shadow Hand, Allegro and Trifinger tasks in IsaacGymEnvs and behind DexTrack; its contact model determines what interpenetration numbers mean.

title: Isaac Lab: A GPU-Accelerated Simulation Framework for Multi-Modal Robot Learning
why: Successor to Isaac Gym/Orbit with the current dexterous task suite, actuator models, sensor simulation and domain randomisation tooling.

title: ManiSkill3: GPU Parallelized Robotics Simulation and Rendering for Generalizable Embodied AI
why: GPU-parallel simulation with rendering, dexterous-hand and bimanual environments, and standardised evaluation; the main open alternative to Isaac for dexterous RL.

title: RLBench: The Robot Learning Benchmark & Learning Environment
why: Canonical 100-task gripper benchmark whose task/demo conventions most later manipulation benchmarks inherit.

title: LIBERO: Benchmarking Knowledge Transfer for Lifelong Robot Learning
why: Canonical imitation-learning benchmark (130 tasks, four suites) used to evaluate VLAs; a reference point for what dexterous benchmarks lack in standardisation.

title: THE COLOSSEUM: A Benchmark for Evaluating Generalization for Robotic Manipulation
why: Systematic perturbation protocol (object, lighting, camera, distractors) with sim-to-real correlation; the template for robustness evaluation of dexterous policies.

title: Robot Learning as an Empirical Science: Best Practices for Policy Evaluation
why: Community position paper on reporting: trial counts, confidence intervals, initial-condition control and qualitative failure description; the basis for the survey's evaluation guidelines.

title: Evaluating Real-World Robot Manipulation Policies in Simulation
why: SIMPLER: shows simulated evaluation correlates with real-world ranking once control and visual gaps are closed; the argument for simulated dexterous evaluation.

title: AutoEval: Autonomous Evaluation of Generalist Robot Manipulation Policies in the Real World
why: Autonomous around-the-clock real-robot evaluation with learned success detection and resets; a route to the trial counts rigorous dexterous evaluation needs.

title: RoboArena: Distributed Real-World Evaluation of Generalist Robot Policies
why: Crowd-sourced pairwise real-world comparison across institutions instead of fixed benchmarks; a scalable protocol for comparing dexterous policies.

title: A Careful Examination of Large Behavior Models for Multitask Dexterous Manipulation
why: Large-scale blind A/B evaluation with sequential statistical tests in sim and real; the most rigorous evaluation protocol applied to dexterous (bimanual) policies to date.

title: Reliable and Scalable Robot Policy Evaluation with Imperfect Simulators
why: Combines many simulated trials with few real trials to give valid confidence intervals on real performance; a statistical framework for sim-heavy dexterous evaluation.

title: Beyond Binary Success: Sample-Efficient and Statistically Rigorous Robot Policy Comparison
why: Sequential tests for policy comparison on continuous quality metrics, not just success rate; supports graded manipulation-quality scoring.

title: Benchmarking in Manipulation Research: The YCB Object and Model Set and Benchmarking Protocols
why: The standard physical/mesh object set and protocol templates used across grasping and dexterous benchmarks.

title: DexYCB: A Benchmark for Capturing Hand Grasping of Objects
why: Hand-object grasp capture on YCB objects with pose-estimation and handover benchmarks; a source of reference grasps for tracking-based dexterous policies.

title: Planning optimal grasps
why: Defines the epsilon and volume grasp-wrench-space metrics still used to score grasps analytically.

title: Grasp quality measures: review and performance
why: Comprehensive review and empirical comparison of analytic grasp-quality measures (contact-point and hand-configuration based); the reference for the metrics section.

title: GRAB: A Dataset of Whole-Body Human Grasping of Objects
why: Whole-body human grasp capture whose mesh-penetration and contact-ratio metrics became the standard physical-plausibility measures for hand-object interaction.

title: Learning Diverse Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Skills from Human Demonstrations
why: BiDexHD turns TACO two-hand demonstrations into 141 simulated bimanual tasks and trains teacher-student policies, reporting 74.6% fulfillment on trained and 51.1% on unseen tasks.

title: Twisting Lids Off with Two Hands
why: Sim-to-real RL for two multi-fingered hands opening bottle lids, showing that a single physics-simulated policy generalises to unseen objects on real hardware.

title: DexMachina: Functional Retargeting for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation
why: Functional retargeting of ARCTIC two-hand demonstrations to several robot hand pairs via RL with decaying virtual object controllers; doubles as a benchmark comparing hand morphologies.

title: ManipTrans: Efficient Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation Transfer via Residual Learning
why: Two-stage imitation (general hand imitator + residual physics module) that transfers bimanual human hand-object motion to simulated robot hands and releases the DexManipNet dataset.

title: Learning Visuotactile Skills with Two Multifingered Hands
why: HATO: low-cost bimanual multi-fingered teleoperation with tactile sensing and diffusion-policy learning of two-hand skills such as handover and pouring.

title: OmniH2O: Universal and Dexterous Human-to-Humanoid Whole-Body Teleoperation and Learning
why: Whole-body humanoid teleoperation with dexterous hands that yields bimanual demonstration data and learned autonomous policies.

title: HumanPlus: Humanoid Shadowing and Imitation from Humans
why: Real-time humanoid shadowing from RGB human pose, then imitation learning of two-hand tasks on a 33-DoF humanoid with dexterous hands.

title: Bimanual Grasp Synthesis for Dexterous Robot Hands
why: BimanGrasp optimises energy-based two-hand grasps verified in Isaac Gym (150k grasps on 900 objects) and trains a diffusion model on them.

title: BiDexGrasp: Coordinated Bimanual Dexterous Grasps across Object Geometries and Sizes
why: Coordinated two-hand grasp generation across object geometries and sizes, the follow-on to BimanGrasp.

title: ArtiGrasp: Physically Plausible Synthesis of Bi-Manual Dexterous Grasping and Articulation
why: Physics-simulated RL policy that synthesises two-hand grasping and articulation of rigid and articulated objects from ARCTIC references.

title: ARCTIC: A Dataset for Dexterous Bimanual Hand-Object Manipulation
why: Mocap dataset of two hands manipulating articulated objects; the reference source for ARCTIC-based retargeting (DexMachina, ArtiGrasp, BiDexHD v2).

title: TACO: Benchmarking Generalizable Bimanual Tool-ACtion-Object Understanding
why: 2.5k bimanual tool-use sequences with hand-object meshes; the demonstration source for BiDexHD's 141 simulated tasks.

title: OAKINK2: A Dataset of Bimanual Hands-Object Manipulation in Complex Task Completion
why: Long-horizon bimanual hand-object task dataset with primitive-level decomposition, used as the evaluation set for DexMan and ManipTrans-style transfer.

title: HOT3D: Hand and Object Tracking in 3D from Egocentric Multi-View Videos
why: Egocentric multi-view dataset with 3D hand and object tracking for both hands from Meta (Aria / Quest 3), a source for egocentric two-hand manipulation learning.

title: GigaHands: A Massive Annotated Dataset of Bimanual Hand Activities
why: 34 hours / 14k clips of markerless bimanual hand-object activity with text annotations, the largest two-hand activity dataset to date.

title: Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware
why: ALOHA/ACT: the canonical low-cost bimanual teleoperation plus action-chunking imitation baseline that most later bimanual dexterous work compares against.

title: RDT-1B: a Diffusion Foundation Model for Bimanual Manipulation
why: 1B-parameter diffusion transformer pretrained on multi-robot data with a unified action space for bimanual control; the reference bimanual foundation policy.

title: GR-Dexter Technical Report
why: Hardware-model-data framework for VLA-based generalist manipulation on a bimanual robot with 21-DoF dexterous hands, the first VLA report at that hand DoF.

title: RoboPianist: Dexterous Piano Playing with Deep Reinforcement Learning
why: MuJoCo benchmark of two Shadow hands playing piano, a high-DoF bimanual coordination testbed with an RL baseline and 150-song suite.

title: RP1M: A Large-Scale Motion Dataset for Piano Playing with Bi-Manual Dexterous Robot Hands
why: One million expert bimanual Shadow-hand piano trajectories generated with optimal-transport fingering, enabling large-scale imitation on RoboPianist.

title: PianoMime: Learning a Generalist, Dexterous Piano Player from Internet Demonstrations
why: Learns a generalist two-hand piano policy from YouTube demonstrations by extracting fingertip trajectories and distilling song-specific RL policies.

title: DexCap: Scalable and Portable Mocap Data Collection System for Dexterous Manipulation
why: Portable two-hand mocap rig with DexIL, which retargets human two-hand demonstrations to a bimanual LEAP-hand robot with human-in-the-loop correction.

title: Bimanual Dexterity for Complex Tasks
why: BiDex: glove-plus-teacher-arm teleoperation for 50+ DoF two-hand systems, shown to collect higher-quality bimanual dexterous data faster than Vision Pro or SteamVR.

title: Open-TeleVision: Teleoperation with Immersive Active Visual Feedback
why: VR-based bimanual dexterous-hand teleoperation with active stereo head tracking, used to collect demonstrations for imitation learning on humanoid arms.

title: DexMimicGen: Automated Data Generation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation via Imitation Learning
why: Extends MimicGen to bimanual dexterous hands with parallel, coordinated and sequential subtask structures; 60 human demos become 21k simulated ones.

title: HumanoidGen: Data Generation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation via LLM Reasoning
why: LLM-reasoned relational constraints over atomic dexterous operations, with MCTS, generate bimanual dexterous demonstrations for a humanoid.

title: Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Based Dexterous Manipulation on Humanoids
why: Sim-to-real RL recipe (real-to-sim tuning, contact-goal rewards, divide-and-conquer distillation) for humanoid two-hand tasks including bimanual handover, with zero-shot transfer.

title: DexMan: Learning Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Human and Generated Videos
why: Converts in-the-wild and generated two-hand videos into simulated bimanual policies without ground-truth poses, evaluated on OakInk2.

title: DexImit: Learning Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Monocular Human Videos
why: Bimanual dexterous policy learning from a single monocular human video, the 2026 step past DexMan/ManipTrans-style mocap-based transfer.

title: AsymDex: Asymmetry and Relative Coordinates for RL-based Bimanual Dexterity
why: Assigns a facilitating and a dominant hand and learns in relative observation/action coordinates, a demonstration-free RL recipe for asymmetric two-hand tasks.

title: Dynamic Handover: Throw and Catch with Bimanual Hands
why: Multi-agent RL for two arm-hand systems throwing and catching, with a learned trajectory predictor for sim-to-real transfer.

title: Learning Dexterous Object Handover
why: RL hand-to-hand object transfer between two multi-fingered hands with a dual-quaternion orientation reward, 94% success on novel objects.

title: DyDexHandover: Human-like Bimanual Dynamic Dexterous Handover using RGB-only Perception
why: Multi-agent RL for dynamic throw-and-catch handover on a dual-arm humanoid with 11-DoF hands from RGB only.

title: LEAP Hand: Low-Cost, Efficient, and Anthropomorphic Hand for Robot Learning
why: The de facto low-cost research hand for learning papers; open hardware, 16 DoF direct-drive Dynamixel, ~$2000, 4-hour assembly, benchmarked against Allegro.
specs: 16 DoF, 16 actuated (Dynamixel XC330 direct-drive at each joint), 4 fingers, MCP kinematics allow abduction at any flexion, ~$2000 BOM, ~600 g, no tactile stock, released 2023 (open hardware, CC/MIT).

title: LEAP Hand V2 Advanced: Dexterous, Low-Cost Hybrid Rigid-Soft Hand for Robot Learning
why: Successor to LEAP with a 3D-printed soft skin over a rigid bone structure and two powered palm articulations; project page https://v2-adv.leaphand.com/ (RSS 2025 demo of v2 precedes it, roboticsproceedings.org/rss21/p132.html).
specs: 17 DoF, five fingers, hybrid rigid-soft (printed soft exterior + printed internal bones), 2 powered palm folds (one across four fingers, one at thumb), ~$3000, released 2025 (open hardware).

title: RUKA: Rethinking the Design of Humanoid Hands with Learning
why: Open-source tendon-driven five-finger hand whose underactuation is made controllable by learned joint-to-actuator and fingertip-to-actuator models from MANUS-glove mocap; the low-cost tendon baseline for humanoid-hand learning.
specs: 5 fingers, 15 joints, 11 actuated DoF (2 per finger, 3 thumb), tendon-driven (Dynamixel in forearm, fishing-line tendons in PTFE, spring extension), ~$1300 BOM, 3D-printed, no tactile stock, released April 2025.

title: Ruka-v2: Tendon Driven Open-Source Dexterous Hand with Wrist and Abduction for Robot Learning
why: Adds a decoupled 2-DoF parallel wrist and finger abduction/adduction to RUKA; reports 51.3% faster completion and +21.2% success on 13 tasks, showing wrist and abduction matter more than raw finger DoF for learned policies (site https://ruka-hand-v2.github.io/).
specs: Tendon-driven, adds 2-DoF parallel wrist (flex/ext + radial/ulnar) and abduction at fingers over RUKA's 11 actuated DoF, 3D-printed, all files open, released March 2026.

title: ORCA: An Open-Source, Reliable, Cost-Effective, Anthropomorphic Robotic Hand for Uninterrupted Dexterous Task Learning
why: ETH SRL's open tendon-driven hand engineered for reliability (popping joints, auto-calibration, tensioning) and validated for 10,000+ cycles; the durability benchmark among open hands, with tactile sensors integrated (site https://srl.ethz.ch/orcahand.html).
specs: 17 DoF, tendon-driven (motors in forearm), integrated tactile fingertips, < 2000 CHF material cost, < 8 h assembly, > 10,000 continuous cycles (~20 h) without failure, 3D-printed, released April 2025 (open hardware).

title: Getting the Ball Rolling: Learning a Dexterous Policy for a Biomimetic Tendon-Driven Hand with Rolling Contact Joints
why: Introduces the Faive Hand (ETH SRL, later commercialised by mimic robotics) with tendon-driven rolling-contact joints and demonstrates zero-shot sim-to-real sphere rotation; the design lineage behind mimic's hand and ORCA.
specs: 11 DoF (v0: 3 fingers + thumb; later 16-DoF versions), tendon-driven with rolling-contact joints and ligament-like constraints, 3D-printable, no tactile stock, released 2023 (open-source sim/hardware).

title: BiDexHand: Design and Evaluation of an Open-Source 16-DoF Biomimetic Dexterous Hand
why: Single-author open cable-driven hand evaluated against the full GRASP taxonomy (33/33) and Kapandji test (9/11); useful as an example of standardised hand evaluation.
specs: 16 independently actuated DoF + 5 coupled joints, 15 servos on cable/pulley N-configuration + one 4-bar joint, 2.14 N fingertip force, lifts 10 lb, OnShape CAD released 2025 (CC BY-NC-SA).

title: DexHand: An Open Source Dexterous Humanoid Robot Hand
authors: Knight (The Robot Studio) and Trevor Blank
why: Fully 3D-printed open-source humanoid hand at ~$300 in parts with ROS 2 drivers and MediaPipe teleop; the entry-level end of the open-hardware spectrum (site https://www.dexhand.org/).
specs: 16 slim micro-servos driving fingers and thumb via tendons, ~$300 USD components, 3D-printed, no tactile, ROS 2 URDF available, released 2023 (v2.x ongoing).

title: Adaptive synergies for the design and control of the Pisa/IIT SoftHand
why: The single-actuator adaptive-synergy hand commercialised as qb SoftHand (qbrobotics); the canonical argument that most grasps need one synergy, not 20 motors.
specs: 19 joints, 1 actuator (adaptive synergy, tendon), rolling-contact joints with elastic ligaments, commercial qb SoftHand Research ~ 0.5 kg, qb SoftHand2 uses 2 motors; released 2014 (research), qb SoftHand commercial since ~2016.

title: Integrated linkage-driven dexterous anthropomorphic robotic hand
why: ILDA hand: all actuation and sensing integrated in the hand via parallel/serial linkages with high fingertip force; the reference for linkage-driven (as opposed to tendon) anthropomorphic design.
specs: 15 DoF, 20 joints, linkage-driven (2-DoF MCP via parallel mechanism, 1-DoF PIP), 34 N fingertip force, 218 mm long, 1.1 kg, fingertip tactile sensing, research prototype 2021.

title: DLR-Hand II: next generation of a dextrous robot hand
why: The classic fully integrated multisensory hand (13 DoF, 6-axis fingertip F/T, Cartesian impedance control) that set the template for DLR/HIT Hand II (Liu et al., IROS 2008, 15 DoF) and modern integrated designs. [SOURCE UNAVAILABLE: publisher paywall, no author-hosted copy found 2026-09-18. Cite by metadata only; no claim in the survey may rest on its contents.]
specs: 13 DoF, 4 fingers, actuators in hand, 30 N fingertip, 6-DoF fingertip force-torque sensors, reconfigurable palm, 12-wire cabling; DLR/HIT Hand II (2008): 5 fingers, 15 DoF, 1.5 kg.

title: DIGIT: A Novel Design for a Low-Cost Compact High-Resolution Tactile Sensor with Application to In-Hand Manipulation
why: The open-hardware vision-based tactile fingertip that fits Allegro fingers and became the default sensor for tactile in-hand manipulation and Sparsh pretraining (manufactured by GelSight).
specs: Camera-based elastomer fingertip, 640x480 at 60 Hz, ~$15 parts at scale, mounts on Allegro, released 2020 (open design; commercial via GelSight).

title: Digitizing Touch with an Artificial Multimodal Fingertip
why: Digit 360: a fingertip with ~8.3M taxels via a hyper-fisheye camera plus microphones, IMU, pressure and heat/odor sensing, released with GelSight; defines what a multimodal fingertip for humanoid hands looks like.
specs: Omnidirectional camera-based dome, ~8.3 million taxels, 7 um spatial features, forces down to 1 mN, on-device AI accelerator, announced Oct 31 2024, commercial via GelSight.

title: Sparsh: Self-supervised touch representations for vision-based tactile sensing
why: First general-purpose encoder family for vision-based tactile sensors (DIGIT, GelSight, GelSight Mini) with TacBench; Sparsh-X (arXiv 2506.14754, 2025) extends it to Digit 360's multisensory streams. GelSight Mini itself has no paper: spec page https://www.gelsight.com/gelsightmini/ (camera-based elastomer, ~32x24 mm gel, USB, ~$500 class, 2022).

title: XELA uSkin magnetic 3-axis tactile skin (Allegro Hand fingertips)
why: Hall-effect 3-axis skin sold as flat and curved fingertip kits for Allegro and other hands; the main non-camera skin in dexterous-hand tactile RL/IL papers (https://xelarobotics.com/products/uscu-alha/).
specs: 3-axis force per taxel, curved fingertip 30 taxels, 0.1 gf resolution, 500 Hz, CAN with ROS/ROS2, full Allegro V4 kit (fingertips + phalanges + palm), commercial since ~2020.

title: PaXini DexH13 tactile dexterous hand and multi-dimensional tactile sensors
why: Chinese hand built around PaXini's own multi-dimensional tactile array (15 sensing dimensions incl. 6-axis force) plus an in-palm camera; CES 2026 'tactile infrastructure' line (https://humanoid.guide/product/dexh13/, PR https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/paxini-unveils-the-tactile-infrastructure-for-embodied-ai-redefining-full-stack-product-matrix-at-ces-2026-302655238.html).
specs: 4 fingers, 16 DoF (13 active + 3 passive), thumb 4 active, 5 kg load, 8 MP eye-in-hand camera, tactile <0.5% FS repeatability, 3 series / 12 models, shipping 2024-2026.

title: Allegro Hand V4 (Wonik Robotics)
why: The workhorse torque-controlled four-finger research hand behind most sim-to-real dexterous RL results (OpenAI-style in-hand rotation, Digit/uSkin tactile work); spec page https://www.allegrohand.com/v4 and wiki http://wiki.wonikrobotics.com/AllegroHandWiki/index.php/Allegro_Hand_v4.0.
specs: 16 DoF, 16 actuated, 4 fingers x 4 joints, direct-drive DC motors with gearing (torque control at 333 Hz over CAN), 0.7 N m joint torque, 5 kg payload, ~1.1-1.2 kg, no tactile stock, ~$20-25k (V4 2016-2024; V5 announced 2024/25).

title: Shadow Dexterous Hand (technical specification, Dec 2024)
why: The 24-joint tendon-driven hand used by OpenAI's Rubik's cube work and most bimanual teleop rigs; the reference for full-anthropomorphism with forearm-mounted motors (https://shadowrobot.com/dexterous-hand-series/).
specs: 24 joints, 20 actuated DoF + 4 coupled, tendon-driven by 20 Maxon motors in the forearm (earlier air-muscle version), 4.3 kg hand+forearm (Lite 2.4 kg), 129 sensors incl. optional BioTac/fingertip tactile, ~$100k class, commercial since 2005.

title: DEX-EE: Shadow Robot hand developed with Google DeepMind
why: Three-finger non-anthropomorphic hand co-designed with DeepMind for uninterrupted RL data collection: overactuated tendons (5 motors per 4-joint finger), 10 kHz force loops, fingertip stereo tactile; the strongest example of designing the hand for the learning loop (https://shadowrobot.com/dex-ee_series/).
specs: 3 fingers, 12 DoF, 15 Maxon DCX16 motors (tendon, >1 motor per joint), fingertip force sensing 0.01-18 N via stereo cameras, 10 N pinch, open-to-close 500 ms, 10 kHz internal force control, released 2024, ~2/3 the price of the Dexterous Hand.

title: Inspire Robots RH56DFX dexterous hand (RH56 series, FTP tactile variants)
why: The cheap 6-motor hand shipped on Unitree G1/H1 and many Chinese humanoids and used across teleop datasets (Open-TeleVision, etc.); FTP variants add fingertip/palm tactile (https://en.inspire-robots.com/product/rh56dfx/).
specs: 12 joints, 6 actuated DoF (6 micro linear servos, linkage), 15 N thumb / 10 N finger tip force, power-off self-locking, RS485/CAN, ~540 g, tactile on RH56DFTP (fingertip+palm arrays), ~$5.5-5.6k, shipping since 2023.

title: PSYONIC Ability Hand
why: Prosthesis-derived hand with fast closing and fingertip touch sensing shipped on Apptronik Apollo demos and many research arms; represents the prosthetic-to-robot crossover (https://www.psyonic.io/robots).
specs: 6 DoF (6 BLDC motors, linkage), 490 g, ~200 ms close, 32 grip patterns, 30 touch values (6 FSR per finger) at up to ~500 Hz over UART/RS485/I2C/BLE, IP64, ~$15-20k, shipping since 2021.

title: ROBOTERA XHAND1 dexterous hand
subtopic: commercial humanoid hand with fingertip tactile
why: Twelve fully active DoF with 270-degree wraparound tactile arrays on every fingertip; used on ROBOTERA's STAR1 humanoid and sold separately (https://humanoid.guide/product/xhand1/).
specs: 12 active DoF (3 thumb, 3 index, 2 each other), direct motor drive, 5 fingertip tactile arrays 12x10 with 3D force + temperature, 80 N grip, 25 kg lift, ~1.1 kg, price on request (~$10k class), shipping since 2024.

title: BrainCo Revo 2 dexterous hand
why: Prosthesis-derived 6-motor hand (Basic/Pro/Touch) adopted by Unitree and others; Touch variant adds multimodal tactile at 0.1 N (https://www.brainco-hz.com/docs/revolimb-hand/en/revo2/parameters.html).
specs: 11 DoF, 6 active joints (tendon/linkage from micro motors), 383 g without wrist, 160 mm, 50 N power grasp, 15 N pinch, 20 kg static load, 0.65 s open/close, RS485/CAN-FD (EtherCAT on Pro/Touch), ~$8.9k MSRP, shipping 2025.

title: LinkerBot Linker Hand L20 (and O6)
why: Chinese full-stack hand vendor with a range from the $1.5k 12-DoF O6 to the 21-DoF L20, all linkage-driven with glove teleop; representative of the 2025 Chinese price collapse (https://openelab.io/products/linker-hand-linkerbot-l20-21, https://www.roboticscenter.ai/hardware/linker-bot-o6).
specs: L20: 21 DoF (16 active + 5 passive), linkage-driven, RMB 49,900 (~$7k). O6: 12 DoF, 16-region tactile, ~$1,500. Shipping 2025.

title: Tesla Optimus hands: Gen 2 (11 DoF, in-hand actuators, 2023) and Gen 3 / V3 (22 DoF, forearm-actuated tendons, patents 2025-2026)
why: Tesla's Dec 2023 Gen 2 hand claimed 11 DoF with tactile fingertips and in-hand actuators (egg demo; https://www.notateslaapp.com/news/1821/tesla-unveils-optimus-robot-gen-2-tesla-designed-fingertip-sensors-actuators-and-ten-other-improvements-video). The Gen 3 / V3 hand moves all actuators into the forearm and drives each finger with three tendons through a crosstalk-managed wrist; the 22 DoF / 50 actuators claim (first shown Oct 2024, detailed in the patent 'Lower robotic arm assembly having a plurality of tendon driven digits') defines the current 'forearm is the hand' direction (https://www.teslarati.com/tesla-optimus-v3-hand-arm-details-revealed-new-patents/, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimus_(robot)).
specs: Gen 2 (Dec 2023): 11 DoF per hand (claimed), Tesla actuators in hand, tactile on all fingertips. Gen 3 / V3 (2025-26): 22 DoF in hand plus wrist, ~50 actuators per arm-hand system (claimed), tendon-driven with 3 tendons per finger from forearm actuators, 4 DoF per finger, tactile fingertips; unreleased, V3 production targeted 2026.

title: Figure 03 hands (palm camera, 3 g fingertip sensitivity)
why: Figure 03 (Oct 2025) ships each hand with an embedded wide-angle palm camera and fingertip pads sensitive to ~3 g; the 16-DoF-per-hand figure is reported by third-party spec trackers, not by Figure's spec card, and should be cited as such (launch page https://www.figure.ai/news/introducing-figure-03; trackers https://humanoid.guide/product/figure-03/).
specs: 16 DoF per hand (third-party reported; not on Figure's spec card), in-palm wide-angle low-latency camera, fingertip pads detecting ~3 g, soft palm; unreleased to third parties, announced Oct 9 2025.

title: NEO's Hands: An API to the Physical World (1X tendon-driven hand)
why: 1X's July 2026 hand is fully force-controlled and backdrivable via low-ratio quasi-direct-drive tendons from the forearm, sealed IP68, with tactile skin on all contact surfaces; the clearest public spec sheet among humanoid vendors (https://www.1x.tech/discover/neos-hands).
specs: 25 actuated DoF (22 fingers+palm, 3 wrist), tendon-driven from forearm, 1X Tendon Drive gear ratio ~5:1-15:1, 45 N distal finger force, 3.5 N m thumb CMC, 2.6 N m MCP, 17.75 N m wrist, +/-0.2 mm accuracy, normal/shear/contact-location tactile skin, IP68 food-safe, wrist tested >2M cycles, stated line capacity 10,000 hands/yr; announced Jul 9 2026, not sold separately.

title: Sanctuary AI Phoenix hydraulic hand (21 DoF)
why: The only humanoid hand using miniature hydraulic valve actuators, claimed an order of magnitude higher power density than cable or electric drives, with valves cycled past two billion times; demonstrated zero-shot in-hand manipilation in 2025 (https://sanctuary.ai/news/sanctuary-ai-demonstrates-in-hand-manipulation-capabilities-for-improved-general-purpose-robot-dexterity/, https://www.automationmag.com/sanctuary-ais-hydraulic-actuation-brings-human-level-dexterity-to-general-purpose-robots/).
specs: 21 DoF per hand incl. finger abduction, miniature hydraulic valve actuation, haptic/tactile sensing (2025 upgrade), valves >2e9 cycles without leak; unreleased (internal to Phoenix Gen 7/8), 2024-2025.

title: Boston Dynamics electric Atlas hands (7-DoF three-finger, production four-digit gripper)
why: Counterexample to the five-finger trend: the electric Atlas used 7-DoF three-fingered hands (2025) and the CES 2026 production Atlas moved to a four-digit (three fingers + thumb) tactile gripper for Hyundai and Google DeepMind deployments (https://bostondynamics.com/blog/boston-dynamics-unveils-new-atlas-robot-to-revolutionize-industry/, https://www.humanoidsdaily.com/news/the-alien-in-the-factory-boston-dynamics-launches-production-ready-atlas-at-ces-2026).
specs: 2025 hand: 3 fingers, 7 DoF, 7 actuators. 2026 production: 4 digits (3 fingers + opposable thumb), tactile sensing in fingers and palm, electric; unreleased, factories 2026-2028.

title: Unitree Dex5-1 / Dex5-1P dexterous hand
why: Unitree's own five-finger hand for G1/H1-2/H2 with 94-point pressure sensing on the P variant; matters because it is what most Unitree-based datasets and policies will run on (https://www.unitree.com/Dex5-1).
specs: 20 DoF (16 active + 4 passive), thumb 4 / others 3, 12 micro force-controlled composite transmission joints (coreless motors + encoders), 1100 g, 10 N fingertip, 3.5-4.5 kg load, +/-1 mm repeatability, 1000 Hz comms, 94 pressure taxels (Dex5-1P), price on request (~$4-5k class), shipping 2025.

title: SharpaWave 22-DoF dexterous hand with Dynamic Tactile Array
subtopic: high-end commercial hand with dense tactile
why: 1:1 human-scale 22-active-DoF hand with 240x240 tactile arrays per fingertip, shipping mid-2026 and chosen as the hand for Apptronik Apollo 2 and Dexmate Vega; the highest tactile density in a commercial hand (https://www.sharpa.com/pages/wave).
specs: 22 active DoF, proprietary actuation modules in hand, 1.3 kg, 208x90x50 mm, 20 N fingertip, 150 N grip, 40 kg payload, 4 Hz gesture speed, DTA 240x240 px per fingertip at 180 fps, 0.02 N resolution, 0-30 N, 6-axis F/T, 500 Hz Gigabit Ethernet, ~$50k reported, shipping since ~June 2026; integrated on Apptronik Apollo 2 and Dexmate Vega.

title: Wuji Hand / Wuji Hand 2: 20-DoF direct-drive dexterous hand
why: Fully direct-drive, backdrivable 20-DoF hand (4 per finger) with MIT-style force-position hybrid control at 1 kHz on every axis; the cleanest example of the direct-drive alternative to tendons (docs https://docs.wuji.tech/docs/en/wuji-hand/latest/overview/, https://www.wuji.tech/en/hand2).
specs: 20 active DoF (4/finger), backdrivable direct-drive rotary joints with FOC, Hand 1 < 600 g / ~15 N fingertip / 10 kg static / +/-1 mm, Hand 2 ~800 g, 1000 Hz x 20 axes, Ethernet/USB/RS485/EtherCAT, no built-in tactile, 300k+ cycles, price on request, shipping 2025 (Hand 2 beta 2026).

title: Proception ProHand 1.0 (22-DoF tendon-driven hand)
why: Ex-Tesla Optimus hand engineers' startup; 22-DoF tendon-driven hand with dense tactile plus a ProGlove for human data, first units shipping June 2026 after settling Tesla's trade-secret suit (https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/R78-proception-the-dexterous-robot-hand-we-wish-existed, https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/29/robot-hand-company-settles-tesla-trade-secret-suit-and-announces-11m-raise/).
specs: 22 DoF, tendon-driven, multi-joint fingers, dense tactile feedback, price undisclosed, $11M seed June 2026, first batch shipping to researchers 2026.

title: Daxo Robotics Muscle V0 (120-actuator compliant tendon hand)
why: Ultra-redundant design with 108-120 backdrivable artificial-muscle tendons and no rigid joints, force-aware touch, built for ~$1,200; V2 slated Q3 2026 (https://www.daxo-robotics.com/, https://humanoid.guide/welcome-muscle-v0/).
specs: 120 actuators / 108 artificial muscles (3x human), tendon-driven, fully compliant (no rigid joints), all actuators backdrivable with force sensing, 100k+ cycle testing, ~$1,200 prototype cost, unreleased (V2 Q3 2026).

title: TESOLLO DG-5F / DG-5F-M / DG-5F-S humanoid robot hand
why: Korean 20-DoF direct-drive hand with fully independent joints and a published catalogue PDF; one of the few high-DoF hands with a public list price (https://www.tesollo.com/products/grippers/dg-5f-m).
specs: 20 DoF (4 independent joints per finger), direct-drive (low backlash), ~200 mm, 1.4 kg (DG-5F-S < 1 kg), 7 kg grip force, EtherCAT, ~$8.8k list, shipping since 2024.

title: Xiaomi next-gen CyberOne bionic hand (22-27 DoF, liquid-cooled forearm)
why: Unveiled at WRC Aug 19 2026 after four months on Xiaomi's car line: adult-male-size hand with 64% more DoF than the prior version, metal-printed micro liquid-cooling channels and evaporative 'sweat' heat rejection in the forearm; 98% success on self-tapping nut installation (https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/3947315943472512, https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/xiaomi-cyberone-humanoid-robotic-hand).
specs: 33 DoF across both hands (66 whole body), reported 22-27 DoF per hand (+64% vs prior), forearm actuation with liquid cooling and evaporative heat dissipation, volume -60% to adult-male size; unreleased, shown Aug 2026.

title: AgiBot OmniHand 2025 / OmniHand Pro 2025
subtopic: low-cost commercial humanoid hand with tactile
why: First sub-10,000 RMB high-DoF hand ('Agile', 16 DoF, 400+ touch points) and a 19-DoF Pro with 0.1 N multimodal tactile; AgiBot spun the hand unit into a separate company in 2025 (https://store.agibot.com/products/omnihand-2025, https://store.agibot.com/products/omnihand-pro-2025).
specs: OmniHand 2025: 16 DoF (10 active + 6 passive), 180 mm, 500 g, 400+ touch points, RMB 9,800. Pro: 19 DoF (12 active + 7 passive), 820 g, 15-25 N fingertip, 35-60 N power grasp, position/normal/tangential/proximity sensing at 0.1 N. Shipping 2025.

title: Clone Robotics hydraulic Myofiber hand (27 DoF)
why: Water-hydraulic artificial-muscle hand on carbon-fibre bones, driven by a 500 W pump through 36 electro-hydraulic valves with a learned neural joint controller; the musculoskeletal extreme of the design space, feeding the Protoclone/Clone Alpha android (https://www.theresarobotforthat.com/clones-robot-hand-has-artificial-muscles/, https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/clone-demos-creepy-humanoid-hand).
specs: 27 DoF, Myofiber hydraulic muscles (up to ~1 kg force each, 650k cycles), 500 W water pump + 36 valves, < 2 lb hand, 70 inertial sensors + palm pressure pads; unreleased (Clone Alpha pre-orders 2025), hand shown 2024.

title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
why: Casts visuomotor policy learning as conditional action diffusion; the default policy head for teleop-collected dexterous-hand data (DexCap, DexUMI, DexWild all build on it).

title: 3D Diffusion Policy: Generalizable Visuomotor Policy Learning via Simple 3D Representations
why: Diffusion policy on sparse point clouds; reports strong data efficiency on multi-fingered hand tasks and is the common 3D baseline for dexterous IL.

title: Universal Manipulation Interface: In-The-Wild Robot Teaching Without In-The-Wild Robots
why: Hand-held gripper with GoPro and SLAM for in-the-wild demonstrations; context for the dexterous-hand analogues DexUMI and DexWild.

title: DexPilot: Vision Based Teleoperation of Dexterous Robotic Hand-Arm System
why: Markerless depth-camera teleop of a 23-DoA Allegro/KUKA system; introduced the fingertip-vector kinematic retargeting cost reused by AnyTeleop and dex-retargeting.

title: AnyTeleop: A General Vision-Based Dexterous Robot Arm-Hand Teleoperation System
why: General camera-based arm-hand teleop across hands and arms; its dex-retargeting library is the de facto open-source hand retargeting toolkit.

title: Holo-Dex: Teaching Dexterity with Immersive Mixed Reality
why: Low-cost VR-headset teleop of an Allegro hand with nearest-neighbour visual imitation; shows an hour of demos suffices for several dexterous tasks.

title: Dexterous Imitation Made Easy: A Learning-Based Framework for Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
why: Single RGB camera hand-pose teleop of an Allegro hand plus nearest-neighbour and BC policies; early evidence that cheap teleop plus simple IL reaches dexterous tasks.

title: Bunny-VisionPro: Real-Time Bimanual Dexterous Teleoperation for Imitation Learning
why: Vision Pro bimanual teleop with haptic feedback and collision-aware retargeting; policies trained from the demonstrations on dual multi-fingered hands.

title: ACE: A Cross-Platform Visual-Exoskeletons System for Low-Cost Dexterous Teleoperation
why: Low-cost hand-arm exoskeleton with camera-based finger tracking, portable across humanoid and arm platforms; a middle ground between gloves and pure vision.

title: DOGlove: Dexterous Manipulation with a Low-Cost Open-Source Haptic Force Feedback Glove
why: Open-source sub-$600 21-DoF glove with force feedback; teleop quality and policy learning compared with vision-only tracking.

title: Towards Human-level Dexterous Teleoperation
why: TeleDexter: 75% success across seven reorientation and tool-use teleop tasks on two dexterous hands, with BC policies trained from the demos; the 2026 state of the art for hand teleop.

title: DexTeleop-0: Force-Aware Bimanual Dexterous Teleoperation with Ego-Centric Perception towards Shared Autonomy
why: Tactile-driven real-time optimisation that turns coarse human tracking into force-compliant bimanual dexterous commands; teleop as a shared-autonomy front end.

title: Geometric Retargeting: A Principled, Ultrafast Neural Hand Retargeting Algorithm
why: GeoRT: a neural human-to-robot hand retargeter trained with geometric objectives, kHz-rate and hand-agnostic; the retargeting layer under DexterityGen.

title: DexMV: Imitation Learning for Dexterous Manipulation from Human Videos
why: First pipeline reconstructing hand-object motion from multi-view human video, retargeting to an Adroit hand, and using it as demonstrations for DAPG-style RL+IL.

title: DexVIP: Learning Dexterous Grasping with Human Hand Pose Priors from Video
why: Uses in-the-wild YouTube hand-pose priors as a grasp-pose reward for RL of a dexterous hand; an early hand-pose-prior route from video.

title: VideoDex: Learning Dexterity from Internet Videos
why: Retargets internet human videos into robot-hand action priors combined with a few real teleop demos; real 16-DoF hand policies for several tasks.

title: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Exemplar Object Trajectories and Pre-Grasps
why: PGDM: shows that a single pre-grasp pose plus an object trajectory is enough supervision for RL to learn 50+ dexterous tasks; the object-centric framing DexTrack later generalises.

title: CyberDemo: Augmenting Simulated Human Demonstration for Real-World Dexterous Manipulation
why: Collects teleop demos in simulation, augments them massively, and transfers to a real dexterous hand; argues augmented sim demos beat more real demos.

title: OKAMI: Teaching Humanoid Robots Manipulation Skills through Single Video Imitation
why: Object-aware retargeting of one RGB-D human video into a humanoid reference plan with dexterous hands, then closed-loop policies from the rollouts.

title: Bridging the Human to Robot Dexterity Gap through Object-Oriented Rewards
why: HuDOR: point-tracked object motion from a single human video becomes a reward for one-hour online fine-tuning of an Allegro hand policy; sidesteps the morphology gap.

title: EgoMimic: Scaling Imitation Learning via Egocentric Video
why: Aria-glasses human egocentric data co-trained with robot data in one policy; the co-training recipe adopted by later dexterous-hand egocentric work.

title: EgoZero: Robot Learning from Smart Glasses
why: Trains deployable manipulation policies from smart-glasses human demonstrations alone (no robot data) using a morphology-agnostic point-based state-action space.

title: Humanoid Policy ~ Human Policy
subtopic: human egocentric data for humanoid hands
why: Human Action Transformer trained on egocentric human demonstrations (PH2D) and transferred to a humanoid with dexterous hands; humans as an additional embodiment.

title: H-RDT: Human Manipulation Enhanced Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
subtopic: human video pretraining / bimanual diffusion transformer
why: Pretrains a 2B diffusion transformer on large-scale egocentric human hand-manipulation data, then adapts to bimanual robots; one of the human-video-pretraining VLA lineages.

title: DexWild: Dexterous Human Interactions for In-the-Wild Robot Policies
why: Glove-plus-wrist-camera rig for collecting human dexterous demonstrations at scale in the wild; co-training with robot data gives cross-scene and cross-embodiment generalisation.

title: DexUMI: Using Human Hand as the Universal Manipulation Interface for Dexterous Manipulation
why: Hand-specific wearable exoskeleton plus video inpainting so a human hand's demonstrations look and act like the target robot hand; policies transfer directly.

title: Dex1B: Learning with 1B Demonstrations for Dexterous Manipulation
why: One billion generated grasping and articulation demonstrations from an optimisation-seeded generative model; scale study for dexterous IL.

title: DexterityGen: Foundation Controller for Unprecedented Dexterity
subtopic: teleop over a learned low-level controller
why: Sim-pretrained motion-primitive controller that a human teleoperator commands at a coarse level; delivers in-hand tool use (screwdriver, syringe) that direct teleop cannot.

title: EgoScale: Scaling Dexterous Manipulation with Diverse Egocentric Human Data
why: Scales dexterous-hand policy training with diverse egocentric human data and studies how data diversity trades against robot data.

title: UniDex: A Robot Foundation Suite for Universal Dexterous Hand Control from Egocentric Human Videos
why: Foundation suite that maps egocentric human hand video to control across multiple dexterous hands; a 2026 attempt at hand-agnostic pretraining.

title: World Models for Learning Dexterous Hand-Object Interactions from Human Videos
why: Learns an action-conditioned hand-object world model from human video and uses it for dexterous robot policy learning; representative of the world-model route.

title: Scaling Cross-Embodiment World Models for Dexterous Manipulation
why: Graph-based world model trained on random interaction data from many simulated hands and real human hands, deployed with MPC on new hardware.

title: pi0: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control
why: Flow-matching action expert on a PaliGemma backbone trained across robots; the reference generalist VLA (laundry folding, box assembly) most dexterous VLAs derive from.

title: pi0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
why: Co-training on heterogeneous web, robot and subtask data to generalise to unseen homes; establishes the recipe later applied to dexterous hands.

title: pi*0.6: a VLA That Learns From Experience
why: RECAP: advantage-conditioned RL from autonomous rollouts and human corrections to improve a deployed VLA; the current pi-series flagship.

title: OpenVLA: An Open-Source Vision-Language-Action Model
why: 7B open VLA trained on Open X-Embodiment; the open baseline for VLA fine-tuning studies, including those on multi-fingered hands.

title: GR00T N1: An Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
why: Dual-system VLA trained on robot data, human video and synthetic data for humanoids with dexterous hands; the open humanoid foundation-model lineage.

title: GR00T N1.6: An Improved Open Foundation Model for Generalist Humanoid Robots
why: Cosmos-2B backbone, 2x larger DiT and thousands more teleop hours; outperforms N1.5 on bimanual YAM, Genie-1 and G1. No paper; landing page only.

title: Helix: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Generalist Humanoid Control
why: Dual-system VLA controlling a 35-DoF humanoid upper body including individual fingers at 200 Hz on onboard GPUs; blog only, cited as industrial evidence.

title: Gemini Robotics: Bringing AI into the Physical World
why: Gemini-2.0-based VLA with demonstrated dexterous bimanual tasks (origami, packing) and cross-embodiment transfer to humanoid Apollo hands.

title: Gemini Robotics 1.5: Pushing the Frontier of Generalist Robots with Advanced Embodied Reasoning, Thinking, and Motion Transfer
subtopic: VLA with thinking and motion transfer
why: Adds embodied reasoning before acting and motion transfer across embodiments; the follow-on that also underlies Gemini Robotics On-Device.

title: Being-H0: Vision-Language-Action Pretraining from Large-Scale Human Videos
subtopic: human-video VLA pretraining for dexterous hands
why: Physical instruction tuning: part-level hand-motion tokenisation and millimetre-level pretraining on human video, then adaptation to a dexterous robot hand.

title: Being-H0.5: Scaling Human-Centric Robot Learning for Cross-Embodiment Generalization
why: Human hand motion as a generalised manipulator template; UniHand-2.0 spans 30 embodiments from dual-arm to legged humanoid.

title: DexVLA: Vision-Language Model with Plug-In Diffusion Expert for General Robot Control
why: Billion-parameter plug-in diffusion expert with embodiment-curriculum training; despite the name, evaluated mainly on grippers and bimanual arms, so cited with that caveat.

title: DexGraspVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Framework Towards General Dexterous Grasping
why: VLM planner plus diffusion controller for a multi-fingered hand; >90% grasp success in cluttered zero-shot scenes.

title: METIS: Multi-Source Egocentric Training for Integrated Dexterous Vision-Language-Action Model
why: Integrates multiple egocentric human and robot sources into one dexterous-hand VLA.

title: Dexora: Open-source VLA for High-DoF Bimanual Dexterity
why: Open-source VLA targeting high-DoF bimanual multi-fingered hands; the 2026 open baseline for bimanual dexterous VLA.

title: H2O: Two Hands Manipulating Objects for First Person Interaction Recognition
why: Egocentric bimanual hand-object dataset with 3D poses and interaction labels; an early two-hands-one-object source.

title: HOI4D: A 4D Egocentric Dataset for Category-Level Human-Object Interaction
why: Large egocentric RGB-D hand-object interaction dataset with category-level object poses and articulated objects.

title: OakInk: A Large-scale Knowledge Repository for Understanding Hand-Object Interaction
why: Object affordance knowledge plus recorded and transferred hand-object interactions; used as a retargeting source for dexterous grasp learning.

title: EgoDex: Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Large-Scale Egocentric Video
why: 829 hours of Vision Pro egocentric video with paired 3D hand and finger tracking across 194 tasks; the scale source for human-video-to-hand policy pretraining.

title: Learning Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
why: First sim-to-real RL for in-hand cube reorientation on a Shadow Hand; established domain randomisation plus massive simulation as the recipe.

title: Solving Rubik's Cube with a Robot Hand
why: Automatic domain randomisation (ADR) curriculum over simulator parameters; the long-horizon sim-to-real showcase for dexterous RL.

title: DeXtreme: Transfer of Agile In-hand Manipulation from Simulation to Reality
why: Reproduces cube reorientation with GPU simulation (Isaac Gym) and vision, cutting compute by orders of magnitude versus OpenAI.

title: DexPBT: Scaling up Dexterous Manipulation for Hand-Arm Systems with Population Based Training
why: Population-based training on Isaac Gym solves regrasping, throwing and reorientation for arm-plus-hand systems; the trainer setup many later papers reuse.

title: Visual Dexterity: In-Hand Reorientation of Novel and Complex Object Shapes
why: Teacher-student distillation to a depth-only policy that reorients novel objects, including downward-facing hand; the standard student-teacher sim-to-real template.

title: In-Hand Object Rotation via Rapid Motor Adaptation
why: Proprioception-only in-hand rotation transferred via rapid motor adaptation; the entry point of the Berkeley/UCSD in-hand rotation line.

title: General In-Hand Object Rotation with Vision and Touch
why: Multi-axis rotation from fused vision, touch and proprioception via a visuotactile transformer; shows touch matters most for physical-property inference.

title: Rotating without Seeing: Towards In-hand Dexterity through Touch
why: Touch-only in-hand rotation with binary contact sensing, sim-to-real; establishes that low-resolution touch is sufficient for rotation.

title: Robot Synesthesia: In-Hand Manipulation with Visuotactile Sensing
why: Represents tactile and visual data as a unified point cloud for RL rotation policies; a clean ablation of sensing modalities.

title: AnyRotate: Gravity-Invariant In-Hand Object Rotation with Sim-to-Real Touch
why: Rotation about arbitrary axes under any hand orientation using dense simulated tactile features, zero-shot to real.

title: Lessons from Learning to Spin "Pens"
why: Dynamic pen spinning via oracle-in-sim, student distillation, then fine-tuning on real rollouts; a candid account of where sim-to-real breaks.

title: DexReMoE: In-hand Reorientation of General Object via Mixtures of Experts
why: Shape-specialised expert policies combined by MoE to raise worst-case reorientation success on 150 objects.

title: DexNDM: Closing the Reality Gap for Dexterous In-Hand Rotation via Joint-Wise Neural Dynamics Model
why: Joint-wise neural dynamics model fitted on little real data adapts a sim policy's actions; rotates high-aspect-ratio and small objects across wrist poses.

title: ViserDex: Visual Sim-to-Real for Robust Dexterous In-hand Reorientation
why: Monocular-RGB reorientation using Gaussian-splat domain randomisation with curriculum RL and teacher-student, trained on consumer hardware.

title: Learning In-Hand Object Reaching to General 6D Poses
why: Sim-to-real RL for reaching arbitrary 6D in-hand poses with an adaptive goal curriculum and a grasp-maintenance reward that lifts real sequence success from 20% to 80%.

title: DexPoint: Generalizable Point Cloud Reinforcement Learning for Sim-to-Real Dexterous Manipulation
why: Point-cloud observations with imagined hand points give category-level grasp and door-opening policies that transfer sim-to-real.

title: UniDexGrasp: Universal Robotic Dexterous Grasping via Learning Diverse Proposal Generation and Goal-Conditioned Policy
why: Two-stage grasp proposal plus goal-conditioned RL policy over thousands of objects; introduces the object-curriculum RL setting later work benchmarks on.

title: UniDexGrasp++: Improving Dexterous Grasping Policy Learning via Geometry-aware Curriculum and Iterative Generalist-Specialist Learning
why: Geometry-aware task curriculum and generalist-specialist iteration raise universal grasp success to ~85% in simulation.

title: Efficient Residual Learning with Mixture-of-Experts for Universal Dexterous Grasping
why: Residual policies over geometry-unaware base experts learn universal grasping in 12 GPU-hours with 88.8% success on DexGraspNet.

title: Dexterous Functional Grasping
why: Eigengrasp action space plus RL to grasp tools in functional poses from internet affordance priors, deployed on a low-cost hand.

title: GraspXL: Generating Grasping Motions for Diverse Objects at Scale
why: RL policy generating physically valid grasp motions for 500k+ objects under multiple objectives, across several hand embodiments.

title: ClutterDexGrasp: A Sim-to-Real System for General Dexterous Grasping in Cluttered Scenes
subtopic: cluttered grasping, teacher RL to student
why: RL teacher in simulated clutter distilled to a 3D diffusion student; first zero-shot sim-to-real closed-loop target grasping in clutter.

title: Closing the Reality Gap: Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Deployment for Dexterous Force-Based Grasping and Manipulation
subtopic: force-based grasping, tactile and motor-current sensing
why: Full-state RL recipe on a 12-DoF hand integrating tactile and motor-current sensing for zero-shot controllable-force grasping.

title: In-Hand Manipulation of Articulated Tools with Dexterous Robot Hands with Sim-to-Real Transfer
why: Sim-trained policies plus sensor-driven refinement operate scissors, pliers and staplers in-hand, extending RL reorientation to articulated mechanisms.

title: SimToolReal: An Object-Centric Policy for Zero-Shot Dexterous Tool Manipulation
why: Procedurally generated tool-like objects in simulation yield a single object-centric policy with zero-shot real performance over 6 tool categories.

title: PhysHOI: Physics-Based Imitation of Dynamic Human-Object Interaction
subtopic: physics-based HOI imitation, contact graph reward
why: Contact-graph reward lets a simulated humanoid imitate dynamic whole-body object interaction; the reward form DexTrack-style trackers inherit.

title: Omnigrasp: Grasping Diverse Objects with Simulated Humanoids
why: A universal dexterous humanoid motion representation lets RL grasp 1200+ objects and follow object trajectories without paired demonstrations.

title: Object-Centric Dexterous Manipulation from Human Motion Data
why: Hierarchical policy: a high-level planner from human hand-object mocap and a low-level RL controller tracking object trajectories, deployed bimanually.

title: DexTrack: Towards Generalizable Neural Tracking Control for Dexterous Manipulation from Human References
subtopic: hand-object tracking control, RL plus IL
why: Generalist tracking controller trained by iterating RL and IL over retargeted human hand-object references; the tracker audited for interpenetration in this survey's own experiments.

title: Dexplore: Scalable Neural Control for Dexterous Manipulation from Reference-Scoped Exploration
why: Single-loop retargeting-plus-tracking where mocap is soft guidance with adaptive spatial scope, scaling across robot hands.

title: TopoRetarget: Interaction-Preserving Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation
why: Retargeting that preserves hand-object contact topology before PPO reference tracking; addresses the contact-structure failure of joint-space retargeting.

title: Learning Complex Dexterous Manipulation with Deep Reinforcement Learning and Demonstrations
why: DAPG: a handful of demonstrations bootstrap policy gradient on Adroit hand tasks; the reference RL+demo hybrid and the origin of the Adroit benchmark.

title: DemoStart: Demonstration-led auto-curriculum applied to sim-to-real with multi-fingered robots
why: Sparse-reward RL with an auto-curriculum over demonstration states solves multi-finger tasks from a few sim demos and transfers zero-shot.

title: Crossing the Human-Robot Embodiment Gap with Sim-to-Real RL using One Human Demonstration
why: A single human RGB-D demo defines object trajectory rewards and initial states for sim RL, then zero-shot real deployment on a multi-finger hand.

title: Eureka: Human-Level Reward Design via Coding Large Language Models
why: LLM-written, evolutionarily refined reward code trains Shadow Hand pen spinning; the reference for automated reward design in dexterous RL.

title: DrEureka: Language Model Guided Sim-To-Real Transfer
why: Extends Eureka to LLM-proposed reward and domain-randomisation configurations for sim-to-real transfer.

title: Deep Dynamics Models for Learning Dexterous Manipulation
why: PDDM: learned dynamics with sampling-based planning rotates Baoding balls on a Shadow Hand; the model-based baseline for dexterous RL.

title: Predictive Sampling: Real-time Behaviour Synthesis with MuJoCo
why: MJPC: real-time predictive sampling solves in-hand cube reorientation without learning; the MPC counterpoint to RL policies.

title: Global Planning for Contact-Rich Manipulation via Local Smoothing of Quasi-dynamic Contact Models
why: Smoothed quasi-dynamic contact models enable RRT-style global planning for in-hand reorientation, explaining why RL's randomised smoothing works.

title: MuJoCo: A physics engine for model-based control
why: The original MuJoCo paper: generalized-coordinate multi-joint dynamics with a convex soft-contact model, the engine behind most dexterous-hand RL and control work for a decade.

title: Convex and analytically-invertible dynamics with contacts and constraints: Theory and implementation in MuJoCo
why: Defines MuJoCo's soft, convex, invertible contact formulation (solref/solimp), i.e. the penetration-permitting contact behaviour every MuJoCo hand result inherits.

title: Simulation tools for model-based robotics: Comparison of Bullet, Havok, MuJoCo, ODE and PhysX
why: The classic head-to-head of five engines on robotics vs gaming tests; MuJoCo wins the robotics (grasp-like) tests, gaming engines the gaming tests.

title: Orbit: A Unified Simulation Framework for Interactive Robot Learning Environments
why: Orbit, later renamed Isaac Lab: modular environments on Isaac Sim/PhysX 5 with rigid, deformable and sensor simulation, the successor to Isaac Gym.

title: NVIDIA Isaac Sim: Enabling Scalable, GPU-Accelerated Simulation for Robotics
why: The Isaac Sim (Omniverse, PhysX 5 GPU rigid bodies) reference paper: the physics and rendering stack underneath Isaac Lab.

title: MuJoCo Playground
why: Environment suite on MJX (MuJoCo on JAX) with a LEAP-hand cube-reorientation task trained in minutes and transferred zero-shot, the MuJoCo-side answer to Isaac Gym.

title: MuJoCo Warp: GPU-optimized version of the MuJoCo physics simulator
why: GPU MuJoCo on NVIDIA Warp reported at 100x speedup on in-hand manipulation; the physics backend of Newton and the drop-in target that ComFree-Sim benchmarks against.

title: Newton: An open-source, GPU-accelerated physics simulation engine built upon NVIDIA Warp
authors: NVIDIA, Google DeepMind and Disney Research
why: The joint NVIDIA/DeepMind/Disney engine with MuJoCo Warp as primary solver, differentiable physics and Isaac Lab integration; where GPU robot simulation is converging.

title: SAPIEN: A SimulAted Part-based Interactive ENvironment
why: PhysX-based simulator with PartNet-Mobility articulated assets; the engine under ManiSkill and much of the DexArt/UniDexGrasp line of dexterous work.

title: ManiSkill2: A Unified Benchmark for Generalizable Manipulation Skills
why: SAPIEN-based benchmark with rigid and MPM soft-body tasks and fast visual observations; the reference point for sample-efficient manipulation simulation before GPU parallelism.

title: Genesis: A Generative and Universal Physics Engine for Robotics and Beyond
subtopic: multi-solver GPU engine (rigid, MPM, FEM, SPH)
why: Unified multi-material GPU engine (rigid, MPM, FEM, PBD, SPH, coupled) claiming tens of millions of FPS; no paper, cited by repository; basis of Tactile Genesis.

title: PyBullet, a Python module for physics simulation for games, robotics and machine learning
why: Bullet/PyBullet: the free CPU engine used by early dexterous-grasp datasets and by TACTO for tactile simulation; a rigid-contact contrast to MuJoCo's soft model.

title: Brax - A Differentiable Physics Engine for Large Scale Rigid Body Simulation
why: JAX-native differentiable rigid-body engine with massively parallel environments; the precursor to MJX and a reference for analytic-gradient RL.

title: Per-Contact Iteration Method for Solving Contact Dynamics
why: The bisection per-contact solver behind RaiSim, a hard-contact, no-penetration alternative to MuJoCo's soft model used for contact-rich legged and manipulation RL. [SOURCE UNAVAILABLE: publisher paywall, no author-hosted copy found 2026-09-18. Cite by metadata only; no claim in the survey may rest on its contents.]

title: An Unconstrained Convex Formulation of Compliant Contact
why: Drake's SAP solver: convex compliant contact with guaranteed convergence and no interpenetration artefacts of penalty methods; the contact model of Drake's hydroelastic grasp simulation.

title: Dojo: A Differentiable Physics Engine for Robotics
why: Hard-contact engine with smooth gradients via an interior-point complementarity solver; a differentiable counterpoint to penalty-based contact for manipulation.

title: DexDeform: Dexterous Deformable Object Manipulation with Human Demonstrations and Differentiable Physics
why: Multi-finger hand and MPM deformable objects in a differentiable simulator with demonstrations; the reference for hand-object interaction with deformables.

title: Contact Models in Robotics: a Comparative Analysis
why: Unified derivation and empirical comparison of the contact models in MuJoCo, Bullet, Drake and RaiSim, quantifying penetration, friction accuracy and solver behaviour.

title: A Review of Nine Physics Engines for Reinforcement Learning Research
why: Recent survey of Brax, Bullet, Chrono, Genesis-era engines, Isaac, MuJoCo/MJX, PhysX, ODE and Drake from the RL-research viewpoint; a table the survey can lean on.

title: ComFree-Sim: A GPU-Parallelized Analytical Contact Physics Engine for Scalable Contact-Rich Robotics Simulation and Control
why: Closed-form contact impulses in Warp with a MuJoCo-compatible API, benchmarked on penetration and friction against MuJoCo Warp and used for real-time MPC on a LEAP hand.

title: TACTO: A Fast, Flexible, and Open-source Simulator for High-Resolution Vision-based Tactile Sensors
why: Render-based simulator for DIGIT and GelSight sensors on PyBullet; the first widely used tactile simulator for grasp learning.

title: Taxim: An Example-based Simulation Model for GelSight Tactile Sensors
why: Example-based GelSight simulation with calibrated optics and marker motion, the usual sim-to-real baseline for vision-based touch.

title: Tactile Genesis: Exploring Tactile Sensors at Scale for Learning Dexterous Tasks
why: Multi-modality taxel simulation in Genesis at 20k parallel environments, 3-20x prior tactile simulators; the current scale point for touch-in-the-loop dexterous RL.

title: dm_control: Software and Tasks for Continuous Control
why: DeepMind's MuJoCo bindings, Control Suite and Composer with the manipulation tasks and Jaco/hand models on which many dexterity baselines are built.

title: Robotic Grasping and Manipulation (book chapter)
venue: RAMSETE: Articulated and Mobile Robotics, Springer LNCIS
why: Bicchi's chapter-length treatment of grasp analysis, form/force closure and hand design; obtained open access and used in place of the paywalled T-RO 2000 paper, which it overlaps but is NOT identical to.
